subject: pe
title: Newton's Laws Applied
welcome_lead: Inertia, F = ma, action–reaction — Newton on the field of play.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on Newton's laws and impulse-momentum in sport.
final_note: Newton's laws are not optional — they govern every block, throw and tackle.

concepts.def: An object continues in its state unless acted on by a resultant force (inertia).
F = ma; force proportional to rate of change of momentum.
Every action has equal and opposite reaction.
p = mv (kg m s⁻¹); vector quantity.
J = F·t = Δp; product of force and time of action (N s).

walkthroughs.body_html: A stationary javelin requires force to move; a moving puck slides forever on frictionless ice.
Greater force at constant mass → greater acceleration. Olympic lifters increase rate of force development to outperform raw strength.
Increasing contact time on landing reduces force experienced (J = Ft); the basis of safe landing technique.

mcqs.q: Newton's third law is invoked when:
options: A sprinter pushes back on the blocks and the blocks push forward
A ball decelerates due to gravity
